text: Private repo created and scaffolded to spec structure (commit 8407ff6)
src/audio_features.py added — resample, log-mel, chroma, segmentation (5 tests, commit 1fa39c7)
src/splits.py added — artist-grouped splitting, no leakage (4 tests, commit f65cec5)
Dataset download instructions documented (commit a231b83)
PROGRESS.md added, GitHub Milestones + Issues created (commit 827ffec)
Deadline corrected to 2026-09-11 (was misread as 2 October)
Rented Vast.ai RTX 4090 instance (24GB VRAM), cloned repo, verified 9/9 tests + CUDA on the fresh environment
Started FMA-medium, FMA-metadata, MagnaTagATune, and DEAM downloads inside a persistent tmux session
MusicCaps' original GitHub source returned 404 — pulled captions CSV from Hugging Face instead (5,521 rows)
Direct YouTube scrape for MusicCaps audio blocked 100% by bot detection — stopped after 42 attempts rather than mislabel live links as dead
Found a pre-scraped MusicCaps audio mirror on Hugging Face (mahendra0203/musiccaps_processed_full) — downloaded and validated 5,355 clips
Built a project status dashboard, first version as a cloud Artifact
Moved the dashboard fully local: python3 http.server + a background polling script on this Mac
FMA-medium finished downloading — 23.8 GB in 34m23s. All four datasets now fully on disk and validated.
FMA-medium integrity check (unzip -tq) started — first attempt's output was lost to a dropped SSH session
Integrity check restarted with nohup to safely capture the result this time
FMA-medium integrity check complete: "No errors detected in compressed data of fma_medium.zip." Confirmed clean.
PROGRESS.md and session log committed and pushed to GitHub (commit 6e6d5b8)
Dashboard upgraded to self-log events instead of static hardcoded entries

Caught a false positive in the auto-logger: it flagged the integrity check as "errors found" because its detection naively substring-matched the word "error" inside the message "No errors detected" — corrected here. The archive is genuinely clean (see 01:53 entry).
Decided to pause for the night. Attempted to back up the 30GB of downloaded datasets before destroying the instance.
Vast.ai's built-in "Cloud sync" defaulted to backing up /workspace/ instead of the actual data directory — caught this before trusting an empty backup.
Corrected the sync path to data/raw/ and retried — throughput collapsed to ~400 KB/s within a minute (Google Drive API throttling)
Tried a direct rsync (instance → Mac) instead — also throttled, ~50-100 KB/s sustained
Isolated the bottleneck with a clean 100MB test file: ~100-200 KB/s sustained after an initial burst — confirmed genuine, not a fluke of either tool
Decided against waiting out the slow backup — re-downloading from original sources next session (~50 min at 15-20MB/s) is cheaper than hours of instance uptime waiting on a throttled transfer
Verified nothing uncommitted or unique was at risk (git status clean except an unused scrape script) — instance destroyed
Decided to switch to Vast.ai persistent Volumes for the next session instead of container disk, to avoid this problem entirely
Rebuilt the dashboard as a full local project command center — state.json + log.json driven, no longer dependent on any live remote instance
Installed vastai CLI (uv tool) and registered API key; switched instance selection from eyeballing the web UI to CLI search with --storage pricing
Destroyed the $0.499/hr RTX 5090 2min after launch — 205GB container disk alone cost $0.067/hr, giving only ~12h runway on $7

CLI revealed storage price varies 3-4x between hosts and is hidden in the web UI. Picked offer 45573262 (RTX 4080S, California): $0.140/hr GPU + $0.005/hr for 90GB = $0.145/hr, 3.4x the runway of the 5090
Created 40GB local volume V.49139226 (22241134_gnnbert_data) on machine 143795, mounted at /data — survives instance destroy, fixing the Aug 24 data-loss problem. Costs $0.111/day billed 24/7

Instance 49139746 up: RTX 4080S 16GB, 64 threads, 62GB RAM (double the advertised 32c/31GB). Image ships Python 3.10.12 + torch 2.5.1+cu121, not the planned 3.12/2.13 — kept the image stack rather than rebuild torch
All 9 Week-1 tests pass on librosa 0.11.0 / Python 3.10 — the version drift from requirements.txt is harmless
All four datasets re-downloaded to /data in 15m50s at ~18MB/s, zero failures. DEAM came straight from cvml.unige.ch this time; MusicCaps again via the HF mirror
Verified + extracted: FMA-small 8000 mp3, MagnaTagATune 25863 mp3, DEAM 1802 mp3, MusicCaps 5355 rows (matches the Aug 24 count exactly). Archives deleted after verification; /data at 17GB of 40GB
Used FMA-small (7.2GB) not FMA-medium (22GB): data/README confirms Task 2 only uses the small subset, and medium would not fit the 40GB volume alongside features

Volume V.49139226 vanished on instance destroy, taking 17GB of verified datasets. Cause: the Vast docs page shows '--env -v V.<id>:/data', which stores the mount as a plain env var and never links the volume
Retried with --create-volume; the volume was destroyed with the instance again. Machine free space went 460GB -> 500GB, confirming release
Ran a controlled persistence experiment with a 1-byte marker file instead of 17GB of data: standalone 'vastai create volume' + '--link-volume' SURVIVES destroy/re-create. Marker read back intact
Volume rule settled: never use --create-volume or --env for mounts. Create the volume standalone, attach with --link-volume. Written into infra/vast-connect.md

'vastai show volumes' and instance volume_info both intermittently report empty for a healthy attached volume. Reliable check is the machine's free volume space via 'vastai search volumes machine_id=143795'
Rebuilt on volume 49151852, sized up 40GB -> 60GB so cached features cannot collide with the 17GB of raw audio

Rewrote update_status.sh: resolves host/port from the vastai CLI instead of hardcoding, tracks all 5 datasets with phase-aware targets, reports volume usage, instance rate/uptime and credit. Fixed an awk 32-bit overflow that capped sizes at 2147483647 and a heredoc/stdin collision that silently blanked every poll
Generalised status.html from a single hardcoded FMA-medium bar to render N datasets from status.json

MagnaTagATune's official mirror (mirg.city.ac.uk) throttled to 68.6 KB/s with an ETA of 2h53m for part 1 of 3 — ~8h total. Almost certainly rate-limited after three pulls of the same archive in one afternoon

Switched MagnaTagATune to the HF mirror confit/magnatagatune: single mp3.zip (2.97GB) instead of 3 split parts, pulled at ~40MB/s — about 600x faster. Also ships the standard MTT train/val/test split TSVs, which the official mirror does not
Volume 49151852 (60GB) seeded and verified: 8000 + 25863 + 1802 mp3, 5355 caption rows, 3 MTT split files, 9/9 tests pass. Machine free space 440GB confirms the volume is registered

THIRD volume loss: standalone create + --link-volume also failed to survive destroy at 60GB/1.5h uptime. The earlier 5GB/2min marker probe that passed was a false positive. Machine free space returned to 500GB and show volumes stayed empty for 3+ min

Abandoned Vast local volumes entirely. With the HF mirror for MagnaTagATune the full seed is ~22min/$0.05, so re-downloading each session costs ~$0.50 over the project vs $1.60 for a volume that does not persist. Irreplaceable artifacts (checkpoints, results, splits) get rsynced down to the Mac instead
